chapter_name: Chapter 11: Integrated Grammar (Gap Filling and Editing)
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will apply their comprehensive grammar knowledge to identify and correct errors in texts and accurately fill structural gaps in paragraphs.]
warm_up_hook: 🕵️‍♂️ Time to put on your detective hat! Integrated grammar is the ultimate test where all the rules you've learned come together. You aren't just learning tools anymore; you are fixing the machine! 🛠️

lesson_modules.teaching_content: When filling blanks, never look at the blank in isolation. Read the sentence before and after it. Look for clues like prepositions that follow the blank, or the tense of the surrounding verbs to choose the right word.
examples_or_templates: Example: 'He is afraid ___ spiders.' (The word 'afraid' is almost always followed by the preposition 'of').
Example: 'Yesterday, she ___ to the market.' (The word 'yesterday' demands the past tense 'went').

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Editing involves finding the error in a line and correcting it. The most common 'suspects' (errors) hide in: Subject-Verb Agreement, Tenses, Articles (a/an/the), and Prepositions.
examples_or_templates: Incorrect: The group of students are waiting. (Subject is 'group', which is singular).
Correct: The group of students IS waiting.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Sometimes a word is missing entirely (Omission). To find it, read the passage aloud in your head. Your brain will often stumble over the exact spot where a conjunction, article, or preposition is missing.
examples_or_templates: Correction: 'I (am) going to school.' (Missing helping verb).

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Choose the best word to fill the gap: 'The children were exhausted because they _____ playing all afternoon.'
❓ Identify the error in this sentence: 'One of the boy was absent today.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Edit the following line by identifying the error and providing the correction: 'There is many stars in the sky tonight.'
subjective_practice.hint: 'Stars' is a plural countable noun. What verb should go with it?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank with a suitable determiner or preposition: 'She has been living in this city ___ 2015, and she knows ___ the best restaurants.'
subjective_practice.hint: Use a preposition of time for the first blank, and a distributive/quantifier for the second.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🩺 The Grammar Doctor
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Take a short paragraph (4-5 lines) from your favorite book. Intentionally introduce 4 grammatical errors (change a tense, mess up an article, remove a preposition). Give it to a friend or family member and see if they can 'diagnose and cure' your paragraph!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Always read the entire passage first to understand the context and overall tense before filling gaps.
⭐ For editing, double-check the 'Big Four': Tenses, Subject-Verb Concord, Articles, and Prepositions.
⭐ Reading sentences aloud in your head helps naturally identify missing words (omissions).
